description: 8 convergence decisions requiring operator ratification before any implementation begins

decisions.question: Which EOS source becomes the canonical main branch?

options.label: Promote Beast feature/company-system
options.description: Beast branch becomes new main. GitHub main archived or rebased.

options.label: Selectively merge Beast to main
options.description: Cherry-pick Beast features into GitHub main. Keep GitHub as base.

options.label: Keep GitHub main, discard Beast
options.description: Treat Beast as experimental. Continue from GitHub main.

options.label: Preserve both temporarily
options.description: Maintain both branches until a later decision point.

decisions.rationale: Beast is 3x larger (603 vs 202 files), already has Clerk auth integrated, company/portfolio/workflow expansion, and represents months of active development. GitHub main is stale (last commit 2026-02-20, all Replit Agent authored). But: require operator review, full test/build validation, secret scan, and rollback plan before promotion. Do not merge blindly.
decisions.risk_detail: Branch divergence is massive — blind merge could break everything. Beast branch has never been CI-validated against main.

decisions.question: What scope defines the CreatorOS MVP?

options.label: Creator/community only
options.description: Minimal scope — creator profiles and community features only.

options.label: Creator + course/product
options.description: Smallest coherent creator OS — content creation, community, and course/product delivery.

options.label: Creator + course + distribution + analytics
options.description: Broader MVP — adds distribution channels and analytics.

options.label: Full PRD scope
options.description: Everything in the product requirements document.

decisions.rationale: Staged MVP approach. Resolve auth bypass vulnerability first — it is a critical security issue that blocks any user-facing work. Smallest coherent creator OS = content + community + courses. Option A is too thin to be useful. Option C/D risks scope creep before foundations are solid.
decisions.risk_detail: Scope creep risk if not gated. Auth bypass must be fixed before any user-facing work. God file splitting needed before feature development.

decisions.question: Which PRD version governs LyfeOS development direction?

options.label: v1.0 canonical
options.description: Original PRD governs. v2.0 shelved.

options.label: v2.0 canonical
options.description: v2.0 replaces v1.0 entirely.

options.label: v2.0 current, v1.0 historical
options.description: v2.0 as current direction. v1.0 preserved as historical context for decisions that led to v2.0.

options.label: Hybrid
options.description: Selectively combine elements from both versions.

decisions.rationale: v2.0 as current direction, v1.0 as historical context. The isolated MVP at lyfeos.net is the current implementation truth. UMH-connected MVP is the future state. LyfeOS is the most mature of the Trinity — clear evolutionary path from v1.0 to v2.0 is valuable context to preserve.
decisions.risk_detail: LyfeOS is most mature with clearest path forward. Risk is minimal.

decisions.question: Which app gets Clerk auth migration first?

options.label: EOS first
options.description: Migrate EOS to Clerk before others.

options.label: CreatorOS first
options.description: Migrate CreatorOS to Clerk first — fix auth bypass vulnerability.

options.label: LyfeOS first
options.description: Migrate LyfeOS to Clerk first.

options.label: All at once
options.description: Parallel migration across all three apps.

decisions.rationale: CreatorOS first because the auth bypass is a critical security vulnerability that must be fixed before any user-facing work. EOS already has Clerk integrated on Beast (just needs branch promotion via DEC-145-001). LyfeOS is the most mature and least urgent for auth changes. Never all-at-once — each migration is independent risk that should be isolated.
decisions.risk_detail: Each migration is independent risk. CreatorOS auth bypass is actively exploitable if deployed. Sequencing reduces blast radius.

decisions.question: How should the cross-Trinity platform standard be created?

options.label: Write from docs only
options.description: Derive standard purely from product documentation.

options.label: Write from docs + code evidence
options.description: Derive standard from product docs AND actual code analysis. Mark implementation deferred.

options.label: Wait until converged
options.description: Defer standard creation until all three apps are converged.

options.label: Avoid standard
options.description: Let each app diverge, no shared standard.

decisions.rationale: Create a planning standard from product docs + code evidence gathered in Phase 14.4/14.4R. Mark all implementation as deferred. Do not extract shared packages yet — that is an implementation concern for post-convergence. The standard is a planning artifact that guides convergence decisions.
decisions.risk_detail: Planning artifact only. No code changes. No risk of breaking anything.

decisions.question: How deeply does UMH integrate with Trinity apps?

options.label: Deep embed
options.description: UMH deeply embedded in each app — shared runtime, shared DB, tight coupling.

options.label: Independent + external orchestration
options.description: Apps fully independent. UMH orchestrates externally via APIs only.

options.label: Hybrid
options.description: Apps own product UX/workflows/business logic. UMH owns orchestration, agents, source truth, production truth, work packets, governance, cross-app intelligence, and operator control.

options.label: No integration
options.description: Trinity apps are standalone. UMH does not integrate.

decisions.rationale: Hybrid boundary. Apps own their product UX, workflows, and business logic — they are products, not UMH modules. UMH owns orchestration, agents, source truth, production truth, work packets, governance, cross-app intelligence, and operator control. This preserves app autonomy while giving UMH the coordination layer it needs.
decisions.risk_detail: Boundary definition only. No code changes. Establishes the contract for all future integration work.

decisions.question: When should shared infrastructure (CI/CD, monitoring, shared packages) be implemented?

options.label: Implement now
options.description: Build shared infrastructure immediately.

options.label: Plan now, implement after convergence
options.description: Create infrastructure plans and specs now. Implement only after convergence plans and app readiness gates pass.

options.label: Defer all
options.description: No infrastructure planning or implementation until apps are converged.

options.label: Deploy immediately
options.description: Deploy infrastructure to production now.

decisions.rationale: Plan now, do not implement. Infrastructure is blocked until convergence plans are ratified and app readiness gates pass. Premature infrastructure wastes resources and creates coupling before the apps are stable. Planning ensures infrastructure is ready to execute when the gate opens.
decisions.risk_detail: Premature infrastructure implementation wastes resources and creates dependencies on apps that are not yet converged.

decisions.question: Should feature building be allowed now?

options.label: Allow now
options.description: Unblock feature development across all Trinity apps.

options.label: Allow LyfeOS only
options.description: LyfeOS is mature enough for feature work. Block EOS and CreatorOS.

options.label: Block all until convergence
options.description: No feature building until convergence decisions are ratified. Allow security-fix planning only.

options.label: Allow security fixes only
options.description: Only security vulnerability fixes permitted. No features.

decisions.rationale: Block all feature build. Allow security-fix planning only. The CreatorOS auth bypass should become a high-priority repair work packet but should NOT be executed in Phase 14.5 — this is a planning phase. Feature development on unconverged codebases creates more divergence. Convergence decisions must be ratified first.
decisions.risk_detail: Correct gate. Blocking features prevents further divergence. Security-fix planning captures the auth bypass without premature execution.

summary.note: All 8 decisions are planning artifacts. Zero implementation is permitted in Phase 14.5. Operator ratification required before any execution phase.
